title: Regenerate lockfiles and enforce ABI/behavioral stability for Python/JS/Go clients
creator: Priya Shah
description: Objective: perform a coordinated dependency bump across Python, JavaScript, and Go language clients, regenerate lockfiles, and introduce an ABI/behavioral stability test harness to prevent regressions when deps or runtime kernels change. This ticket covers cross-language policy, release gating, and a zero-downtime rollout strategy for deprecating legacy API fields.
acceptance_criteria: All three language clients (python, js, go) have regenerated lockfiles and use pinned transitive versions consistent with the curated dep matrix.
A cross-language regression test harness exists that validates (a) public API surface responses, (b) streaming behavior, and (c) embedding/encoding compatibility across client versions.
CI gates will fail when a PR introduces a behavior change vs. a canonical golden set for each client; exceptions require a documented migration plan and approval.
No end-to-end customer-facing breakage observed in the canary group (internal apps + 5 external beta customers) during a 72-hour burn-in after rollout.
Documentation updated: migration notes for deprecated fields, examples for new transport behavior, and CHANGELOG entries per client.
Automated release artifacts (wheel/tarball/npm tgz/go binary) signed and published to our internal registry with backward-compatibility notes.
Security review required signoff obtained for any dependency with CVE warnings prior to release.
